readme.html:
bc-word-layout-mcp

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI agents create, edit, validate, and preview Microsoft Word report layouts for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central through deterministic, typed tools — instead of free-hand OOXML editing, which is unreliable in a file format where a single misplaced element silently corrupts the document.

28 typed MCP tools over stdio: inspect any layout, validate it (structurally, and via a real dry-run merge), render an offline mock PDF preview the agent can look at, and author edits — fields, labels, repeater tables, nested detail rows, block repeaters, table structure, text and cell formatting, full lifecycle refresh. One uniform response envelope; nothing throws across the MCP boundary; every mutating edit is validated before it is saved and rejected outright if it would corrupt the file.

  • skills/al-word-layout/SKILL.md — the companion skill: the intended agent workflow (inspect → edit → validate → preview → sandbox verify).
  • skills/al-word-layout-design/SKILL.md — the design skill: what a new layout should look like — archetype skeletons and observed BC document conventions, each tagged with the stock corpus layout or BC-verified build it comes from.
  • skills/al-word-layout-from-design/SKILL.md — from a finished Word design plus the report's empty layout to a bound layout: what to ask a consultant for, mapping sample text to dataset fields, binding it, checking it.
  • skills/al-word-layout-composite/SKILL.md — composable layouts: what the body, header/footer and theme files contain, and the style contract between them.
  • docs/SOLUTION-DESIGN.md — architecture and design rationale.
  • docs/adr/ — the deliberate design decisions, as ADRs.

Install

The server reads and writes layout files with your own permissions, at paths the calling agent supplies — point it only at repositories and layouts you trust, as you would any local build tool.

Option A — NuGet package via dnx (needs the .NET 10 SDK)

The .NET 10 SDK ships dnx, which fetches and runs the packaged server on demand — no install step, version-pinnable.

VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json, or user-level mcp.json):

{
  "servers": {
    "bc-word-layout": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "dnx",
      "args": ["BcWordLayout.Mcp", "--yes"]
    }
  }
}

Claude Code (.mcp.json in a project, or user scope via the one-liner):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bc-word-layout": {
      "command": "dnx",
      "args": ["BcWordLayout.Mcp", "--yes"]
    }
  }
}

claude mcp add bc-word-layout -- dnx BcWordLayout.Mcp --yes

Unpinned, dnx resolves the latest stable release at each launch, so updates arrive without config edits. Append an exact version — BcWordLayout.Mcp@1.2.3 — to pin for reproducibility; a pinned config stays on that version until you edit it. Pinning is also the only way to run a pre-release, which latest-stable resolution skips.

Prefer a pinned global install over on-demand fetch? dotnet tool install -g BcWordLayout.Mcp installs the same server as the bc-word-layout-mcp command; use that as the command in the blocks above (no args).

Option B — self-contained binaries (no .NET required)

Each GitHub Release carries win-x64 and win-arm64 zips (the whole publish folder — the exe does not run alone) plus an install script that unpacks to a stable location, verifies the checksum, and prints the ready-to-paste config block:

irm https://github.com/TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

For a specific version, pre-releases included, run that release's own script with -Version:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://github.com/TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp/releases/download/v1.2.3/install.ps1))) -Version 1.2.3

The documented config then points at the fixed path %LOCALAPPDATA%\bc-word-layout-mcp\current\BcWordLayout.McpHost.exe.

Option C — from source (contributors)

The repo-root .mcp.json launches the server from your working tree with dotnet run --project src/BcWordLayout.McpHost --artifacts-path .mcp-run, so there's no publish step while iterating. The separate .mcp-run/ build folder matters on Windows: a running server locks the DLLs it loaded, and building into the normal bin/ folders would stop dotnet build and dotnet test while any session is open.

Claude Code starts every .mcp.json server when a session opens, whether or not it's used. So the committed .claude/settings.json lists this one in disabledMcpjsonServers, and sessions in the repo don't start it. To use your build as a server, add it under your own local scope, which that setting doesn't cover:

claude mcp add --scope local bc-word-layout-dev -- dotnet run --project src/BcWordLayout.McpHost --artifacts-path .mcp-run

Remove it again with claude mcp remove --scope local bc-word-layout-dev. Either way, the server runs the code as built when the session started; restart the session to pick up later edits. See Building from source.

The companion skills and plugin

Four skills ride along with the server: al-word-layout teaches an agent the intended workflow and the supported matrix, al-word-layout-design teaches what a from-scratch layout should look like (archetype skeletons and observed BC document conventions), al-word-layout-from-design turns a finished Word design plus the report's empty layout into a bound layout — so a functional consultant can get a working layout without touching OOXML or AL — and al-word-layout-composite covers composable layouts: the report body, the reusable header/footer layout and the theme. The server is fully usable without them, but agents drive the tools noticeably better with them. The plugin installs the skills and the server entry together, and this repository is a plugin marketplace for both ecosystems:

  • Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp, then install the bc-word-layout plugin it offers.
  • VS Code / GitHub Copilot (agent plugins, preview): add "chat.plugins.marketplaces": ["TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp"] to your user settings.json, then install the bc-word-layout plugin from the marketplace. The same mechanism serves Copilot CLI.
  • Manual copy (the floor — no plugin system involved): copy the skills/ folders (al-word-layout/, al-word-layout-design/, al-word-layout-from-design/, al-word-layout-composite/) into your project's .claude/skills/ or .github/skills/ (or user-level ~/.claude/skills/). SKILL.md agent skills are an open standard — Claude Code, VS Code, and Copilot CLI all scan these locations natively; the server is then registered separately per Option A/B above.

Configuration (optional)

Label classification works out of the box for both shapes found in real BC layouts: columns whose name ends in Lbl/_Lbl (BC's documented convention), plus every direct column of a data item named Labels — a dedicated labels data item, common in older/converted reports whose columns are suffixed Caption/Label or not at all. The second rule is self-scoping: it only affects layouts that actually contain a Labels data item, so no per-report configuration is needed. Two environment variables override this default convention, read once at server startup; an invalid value is ignored (logged to stderr) and the default kept:

  • BCWL_LABEL_SUFFIXES — comma-separated label suffixes, e.g. Lbl,Caption (default: Lbl).
  • BCWL_LABELS_DATA_ITEM — retargets the labels data-item rule to a different data-item name, or disables it entirely with the special value - (default: Labels).
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bc-word-layout": {
      "command": "dnx",
      "args": ["BcWordLayout.Mcp", "--yes"],
      "env": {
        "BCWL_LABEL_SUFFIXES": "Lbl,Caption",
        "BCWL_LABELS_DATA_ITEM": "ReportLabels"
      }
    }
  }
}

Supported platforms

Windows (x64 / arm64) is the supported platform. PDF preview conversion uses Microsoft Word via COM automation when Word is installed. A LibreOffice converter (soffice CLI) exists in the code as the fallback and is what non-Windows use would rely on — but it is untested and unverified end to end, so Linux and macOS are currently unsupported, not "supported via LibreOffice" (the non-Windows code paths compile and their unit tests run in CI as a rot-guard; that is a build claim, not a support claim).

Neither Word nor LibreOffice is required to use the server. Without a converter, preview_layout still merges the sample data and returns the merged .docx path — it reports conversionOk: false with a conversionError explaining why, instead of failing the call (and removes the PDF an earlier preview left, so no stale render remains next to the new merge). Every other tool is conversion-free and works everywhere the server runs.

Tools

Tool Purpose
get_layout_info Inspect a layout: report name/id, dataset namespace, storeItemID, the full control inventory (kind, alias, tag, xPath, part, parent repeater), per-part details (kind, header/footer role default/first/even, and which part a partName-less header/footer edit targets) plus a hasTitlePage flag, every table's rows (one per w:tr, so each row of a multi-row repeater item is addressable, tagged with the repeater it repeats with) and cells — each cell with both its physical colIndex (what the cell tools take) and its gridColumn/gridSpan (what the column tools take; they differ on any spanned row), each row with its gridBefore/gridAfter — and a quick validation summary.
list_dataset_fields List the dataset hierarchy (data items + columns) from a .docx layout or a standalone schema .xml; flags labels and, for a layout, bound/unbound columns.
validate_layout Validate a layout: level=quick (structural + binding checks, including a repeater-downgraded error for a repeater a Word save turned into a plain content control, a top-level-repeater-group error for a block-level repeater over the top-level data item without the w:group wrapper Business Central needs to print it, an attached-template error for a layout that links an external Word template (Business Central refuses to upload one), a warning when a layout containing repeaters declares a Word compatibility mode below 15, a duplicate-control-id warning when two content controls share a w:id, and a font-installed warning for a font Business Central online does not have) or level=full (adds a dry-run merge that surfaces every unresolved binding as a finding).
preview_layout Mock preview: merges deterministic (or supplied) sample data into a working copy and converts it to PDF via Word COM or LibreOffice.
render_preview_pages Render pages of a preview PDF (the pdfPath from preview_layout) as PNG images returned inline as MCP image content blocks, so the calling agent can visually inspect the preview (default 3 pages, cap 10 per call; page onward via firstPage; each page capped at 5000 px a side and 20 MP, a larger one rendered smaller and flagged downscaled). Pass outputDir to also write each page as a .png a human can open — optionally with inlineImages=false to skip the token cost of the inline copies.
create_layout Create a new blank layout .docx from a schema, optionally starting from a branded/styled (unbound) template. A blank build ships deterministic default typography (Calibri 11 pt via a scaffolded styles part) so it renders with the same font in Word and in BC, plus a settings part declaring compatibilityMode 15 so its repeaters survive being opened and saved in Word.
insert_field Insert a plain-text FIELD content control bound to a dataset path, in the body, a header, or a footer.
insert_label Insert a plain-text LABEL content control bound to a label-suffixed (Lbl/_Lbl) dataset path.
insert_text Insert plain STATIC text — a literal run, not a content control: the separator space, colon or " / " that glues two inline controls together (without it, chained controls render as Document NoDOCU-0150). Creates no control, so it has no controlId and cannot be targeted by remove_control.
insert_page_number Insert Word PAGE/NUMPAGES field codes — the "Page X / Y" chrome every stock BC document header carries (by default the full X / Y shape; includeTotal=false for the current page alone). Field codes are plain runs, so no controlId.
insert_repeater_table Insert a complete repeater table (label/static header row + one bound data row) for a repeating data item, in the body — the flagship editing tool. Draws the BC-native look by default (no grid, one rule under the header row; borders also offers none or a full grid) and can reference a table style the layout defines; optional per-column widths and alignments, pinned with a fixed table layout so Word renders the grid as specified.
insert_repeater_row Add a nested DETAIL ROW repeater inside an existing repeater's item — the standard BC shape for per-line detail (assembly components, serial/lot nos): a row under each line, aligned to the parent grid via spans, repeating once per parent row. Its cells take the run formatting and paragraph style of the row above them, column by column; format overrides.
insert_picture Insert a PICTURE content control bound to a picture dataset path (e.g. /Header/CompanyPicture) — the logo placeholder a from-scratch layout needs; BC fills it at render time.
insert_table Insert a plain (unbound) table, in the body, a header or a footer — the building block for non-repeating layout sections (address columns, label/value header grids, right-anchored totals blocks, the stock header and footer tables). Borderless by default, with the same borders and tableStyle options as insert_repeater_table. Column widths are pinned with a fixed table layout, so Word keeps the grid you asked for. Returns the new table's index for set_cell_text/insert_field to fill.
wrap_in_repeater Wrap a run of existing body blocks in a block-level repeater over a data item, so they print once per record: a page per customer in a statement, a paragraph per work-description line. Over a top-level item it adds the w:group Business Central needs; over a nested item, a paragraph holding only a field becomes a block-level field control, the shape Business Central prints.
remove_control Remove a content control (field/label/repeater/picture/unbound) by its w:id, searching the body and every header/footer; keepText=true on a block-level repeater unwraps it and keeps its content.
set_cell_text Set (replace) the PLAIN TEXT of a table cell, addressed by table/row/column index — e.g. re-label a line-items column header. Rejects cells that hold a bound control.
set_text_format Restyle text that is ALREADY in the layout without changing it: a control by id, a table cell, a whole row, or one exact piece of text, with the same format object the insert tools take (bold, italic, underline, size, font, colour, character style) and an optional alignment.
clear_cell_text Remove all PLAIN TEXT from a table cell, leaving a valid empty cell (the cell/column is preserved) — e.g. blank an unwanted column-header label.
insert_subtotal_row Append a STATIC per-group row at the end of an existing repeater's item — the stock BC shape for group subtotal (and spacer) rows: it renders once per PARENT row, after the nested detail rows, never per detail row. Its cells take the formatting of the row above them, as insert_repeater_row's do.
insert_table_row Insert ONE STATIC (non-repeating) row into an existing table — the stock BC shape for the totals block INSIDE the line-items table (spacer cells, a spanned bound caption cell, a right-aligned bound amount cell). Cells bind FULL dataset paths; the row renders exactly once, never per data row. Its cells take the formatting of the row above them (below, at the top of a table), as insert_repeater_row's do.
set_column_widths Set a table's column widths (one twip value per grid column); gridSpan-aware — each cell is resized to the sum of the columns it spans.
insert_column Add a new column at any grid position (append by default) — a bound field/label cell (as insert_field/insert_label) or a plain-text column. Adds the w:gridCol and one cell per row; a spanned cell in a row with no content there is widened instead. The table keeps its total width: the new column's width comes out of the existing columns.
remove_column Remove a whole grid column — addressed by the gridColumn get_layout_info reports for its cells, not their colIndex: drops each row's covering cell (a bound cell too) or decrements its gridSpan, and removes the w:gridCol. The summary says per row which of the two happened.
merge_cells Horizontally merge a run of adjacent cells in one row into a single gridSpan cell (keeps the first cell's content).
split_cells Horizontally split one spanned cell back into single-column cells.
set_cell_format Set the appearance of a whole row's cells, or one cell: the per-cell rules a BC document's look is actually made of (a line above a totals row, an underline on one cell) and/or a fill colour (a shaded header row).
refresh_xml_part Update a layout's BC dataset XML part to a new schema in place; remaps/orphans bindings, re-points any binding left naming a foreign report's namespace (which BC refuses to upload) or a storeItemID that names no part, and reports newly-unbound fields. Also the repair for a dataset part that no longer parses (validate_layout names the part and the parser error).

Response envelope

Every tool returns a uniform envelope:

{ "ok": true, "data": { "...": "tool-specific payload" } }

Members that would be null are omitted rather than sent as null: a success has no error key, a failure has no data key, and an optional field inside data is simply absent.

One tool extends (never replaces) this shape: render_preview_pages returns the same JSON envelope as its result's first text content block, followed by one MCP image content block per rendered page — the only way a tool result can carry images over MCP. Its envelope JSON is serialized with the same options the SDK applies to every other tool, so parsers see an identical shape either way.

On failure, error is populated with { code, message, hint } — hint is always a non-empty, agent-actionable next step (which argument to fix and its valid values, or which inspection tool to call first). Nothing throws across the MCP boundary. The 22 mutating tools (insert_field, insert_label, insert_text, insert_page_number, insert_picture, insert_table, insert_repeater_table, insert_repeater_row, insert_subtotal_row, insert_table_row, wrap_in_repeater, remove_control, set_cell_text, set_text_format, clear_cell_text, set_column_widths, insert_column, remove_column, merge_cells, split_cells, set_cell_format, refresh_xml_part) additionally run OpenXmlValidator before saving — a write that would introduce a new structural error is rejected (edit_would_corrupt) and the file on disk is left untouched. Every one of them is also checked by a grid-consistency guard that rejects (edit_would_break_table, file untouched) any edit leaving a row's cells inconsistent with its w:tblGrid — a corruption class OpenXmlValidator accepts silently. Every save also removes a link to an external attached template, which Business Central refuses to upload, and the summary says so. Every successful mutating response also carries a fresh post-edit quickValidation summary. (create_layout writes a new file instead: it checks the layout it built and returns quickValidation too, but a failure of that check is a server bug, reported as internal_error, never edit_would_corrupt.)

Envelope boundary: malformed calls get the envelope too. The SDK looks the tool up and binds the JSON arguments onto its typed parameters before any tool body runs. The server's call-tool filter wraps that step, so a call that never reaches a body still returns isError: true with the same {ok:false,error:{code,message,hint}} shape:

  • Unknown tool name: invalid_argument naming the tool; the hint points at tools/list.
  • Missing required argument: invalid_argument naming it; the hint lists the tool's required parameters.
  • Wrong JSON type ("abc" or 1.5 for an integer, "true" for a boolean, null for a number or boolean): invalid_argument naming the parameter, the type it needs, and what the call sent. Inside an object or array argument it names the member or item by its path (columns[1].width), or the required member an object lacks.
  • Unknown argument name: refused with invalid_argument rather than ignored, naming the closest real parameter (layoutpart → layoutPart; names are case-sensitive) and listing them all. An ignored misspelling would silently fall back to the parameter's default. The same holds for the members of an object argument and of the objects in an array (format.size, columns[1].Width).
  • Object or array sent as a JSON string ("[1500, 6206]" for [1500, 6206]): read as the value it holds, since the string is unambiguous. A comma-separated list is not a JSON array and is refused, with a hint that asks for one.
  • Relative path: every path parameter must be absolute; a relative one (or a drive- or root-relative one like C:Report.docx) is refused with invalid_argument naming the parameter, instead of resolving against the server's working directory.
  • Explicit null for a string: an optional enum-like string (layoutPart, borders, borderStyle, converter, level) takes its documented default, exactly as if it were omitted; a required one (locationType, mode) is refused with invalid_argument.

The input schemas say what an argument may hold before any call is made: every enumerated argument lists its values (enum) and every bounded number its range (minimum/maximum), including the members of format and of the table tools' column and cell objects. The server still reads an enumerated value case-insensitively.

Only a request too malformed for the SDK to parse as a tool call at all (no tool name, or arguments that is not a JSON object) fails earlier, as a JSON-RPC error with no tool result; MCP client libraries do not produce that shape.

Mock preview: not a substitute for a sandbox render

preview_layout merges deterministic sample data (or a real dataset via dataOverridesPath — both the layout's own data-store part shape and the report UI's Send to → XML export are accepted, and the export's decimalformatter columns are formatted the way BC itself renders them) into a working copy of the layout and converts it to PDF entirely offline — never through the real Business Central report engine. That's good enough to catch structural and binding mistakes on every edit, but captions, fonts, and exact pagination can differ from a genuine BC render. Every preview_layout response repeats this as a disclaimer string. A dataset printed for several documents previews only the first, and a multiple-top-level-records warning says so: BC renders the report body once per top-level record, the mock does not. Generated sample data fills every field and every repeating item, so the mock cannot show a field that is empty in real data (a purchase order's VendAddr block previews full and prints empty), and it ignores the BC add-in's hide-if-empty controls, which do hide content in BC.

Final sign-off on any layout is always a real Business Central sandbox render (AL build → publish to dev sandbox → run the report), never this tool's PDF alone.

What has been validated against a real Business Central sandbox: packs of layouts made with these tools were uploaded to real BC sandboxes and rendered by the real report engine, in three rounds on BC 28 (Cronus AU). Rounds 1 and 2 (2026-08, BC 28.0 and 28.3) had five items, then seven, three of them from-scratch builds, and every item passed. Round 3 (2026-10) printed seventeen items covering what 2.0 writes, plus seven follow-up probes, and found four things the tools got wrong: a link to an external template that BC 28 newly refuses on upload, a template conversion that crashed BC's print, a detail row's formatting, and a work-description repeater shape BC did not print. Each is fixed in 2.0.0 and printed correctly again. Round 3 also measured three behaviours the project had no evidence for: last-page-only field codes, a storeItemID naming no part, and the add-in's hide-if-empty controls. docs/FIDELITY-CHECKLIST.md records every round and what it measured. BC accepts what these tools author, bindings resolve, repeaters expand, and the mock preview's structure matched the real render on the dimensions checked. That is what it proves — and no more: one BC version family, one localization, the layouts in the pack. The mock preview remains a mock; the per-release fidelity procedure and its open manual dimensions live in the same checklist.

Public contract and versioning

This project follows semver. From v1.0.0 on, the public API is: tool names, tool parameters (names, types, required-ness), the {ok, data, error} envelope shape, and the error codes. Removing or changing any of those is a breaking change and lands only in a major version; new tools, new optional parameters, new data fields, and new error codes are additive (minor). Error message/hint texts are not part of the contract — never parse them.

  • Business Central versions: validated against BC 28: 28.0 and 28.3 in rounds 1 and 2, a BC 28 sandbox in round 3 (see above). Word report layouts are a long-stable BC format, so the tools are expected to work with any BC version that supports Word layouts — reports of issues on other versions are welcome — but the compatibility commitment extends only to versions a validation has actually covered.
  • MCP SDK cadence: the server pins an exact version of the official ModelContextProtocol C# SDK (the host's project file names it) and upgrades it in minor releases, with any behavioral consequence called out in the changelog. The envelope boundary above is pinned by a host-level test that runs the real server pipeline over the SDK's own transport, so an upgrade that changes it fails the suite.

Not supported

  • Hide-if-empty BC add-in conditional controls (Hide Field if Zero, Hide Empty Table, Hide Empty Table Row, layout comment) — no set_hide_if_empty tool yet. What BC 28 does with the two captured ones is measured (#123): inside a repeater, Hide Table Row If Empty hides the whole repeated item when its cell is empty, and outside a repeater it does nothing; Hide Table If Empty around a cell does nothing. A tool is planned after 2.0; until then a hand edit in the captured shape works. Hide Field if Zero and layout comments wait on capturing the BC Word add-in's OOXML (#8, ADR-0005).
  • Page-position-conditional content (IF PAGE = NUMPAGES, e.g. text on the last page only) — no tool yet. Business Central evaluates the field per page, as Word does (sandbox-verified on one- and two-page documents), and a tool is planned after 2.0 (#11); until then a templatePath shell or a hand edit carrying it works.
  • Repeaters in headers/footers — nothing shows that BC renders a repeating section there, so insert_repeater_table only creates one in the document body and wrap_in_repeater only wraps body content; a pre-existing/hand-authored one is still detected by validate_layout with a warning rather than silently accepted. (NESTED repeaters in the body are supported: insert_repeater_row adds the standard detail row under each parent line, or insert the inner table into a cell of the outer table's dataRowIndex row.)
  • Real XLF caption translations — not planned. With generated sample data, preview_layout fills labels from the dataset's own label columns, falling back to humanized element names, so captions read differently from a real BC render. Pass a real exported dataset via dataOverridesPath when caption text matters: the dataset carries BC's own captions, and they then match the real render.
  • Table-structure changes — largely supported (insert_column, remove_column, set_column_widths, horizontal merge_cells/split_cells — all gridSpan-aware, grid-column-addressed, guarded against desyncing a row from its w:tblGrid; rows skipping grid columns via w:gridBefore/w:gridAfter are handled). Still deferred and refused with a clear message, pending real-add-in OOXML capture: any table using vertical merges (w:vMerge) — except set_cell_format, which is cosmetic and accepts them. See issue #9.
  • Cosmetic formatting beyond text and cells (margins, page setup, styles/branding) — no dedicated tool. Text has the format object (bold, italic, underline, size, font, colour, character style) on every tool that writes it, plus set_text_format to restyle text already in the layout; cells have the alignment arguments and set_cell_format's rules and fills; and a blank create_layout ships deterministic default typography (Calibri 11 pt via its scaffolded styles part). For the rest, restyle via create_layout's templatePath or hand-edit the OOXML directly, then run validate_layout to confirm the edit didn't break structure or bindings. Restyling in Word is safe for a layout this tool created — it declares compatibilityMode 15, so Word preserves the repeating sections; a layout that declares a lower mode (an older build, or a templatePath shell that brought one) loses them on save, which is what validate_layout's compatibility-mode warning is for.
  • Generating the dataset schema itself — deliberate, not a gap (ADR-0006): create_layout and refresh_xml_part take their schema from a BC-produced artifact (a compiler-generated layout, an exported stock layout, or an exported schema .xml) and transplant its part content byte-for-byte, so "the layout's XML part == the compiler's XML part" holds by construction. Reimplementing the AL compiler's dataset-to-schema mapping (element-name derivation, IncludeCaption → _Lbl columns, namespace construction) would reintroduce exactly the drift class the transplant rule eliminates. Practical consequence: a brand-new layout starts with one AL build (the compiler creates the referenced layout .docx, dataset part included) or one export from BC — the skill's §1 documents the workflow.
  • RDL layouts, Excel layouts — out of scope entirely; this server is Word-only.
  • Any BC-connected upload of a layout to a tenant — no public API exists for this; it is UI-only in Business Central, a deliberate scope decision rather than a gap to script around.

Building from source

Prerequisite: the .NET 10 SDK (and the nuget.org package source configured).

dotnet build     # warnings fail the build (TreatWarningsAsErrors + .NET analyzers)
dotnet test

The suite includes Word COM PDF-conversion tests and OOXML snapshot tests against the corpus of 10 real BC layouts (tests/corpus/ — see PROVENANCE.md). The PDF-converter tests are dependency-agnostic: they pass whether or not Word/LibreOffice is installed (an unavailable converter is itself a tested, expected outcome, not a skip).

Publish a self-contained executable

dotnet publish src/BcWordLayout.McpHost -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained

Produces BcWordLayout.McpHost.exe (~160 KB) in src/BcWordLayout.McpHost/bin/Release/net10.0/win-x64/publish/ alongside the rest of a self-contained deployment (240 files, ~109 MB — the .NET 10 runtime plus every dependency, so the target machine needs no .NET installed; native debug symbols are stripped at publish). Ship the whole publish/ folder together, not just the .exe — it depends on the sibling .dlls. scripts/build-release-zips.ps1 builds the exact per-RID zips (+ checksums) a GitHub Release carries, and python tools/release/verify_server.py -- <command> smoke-tests any install channel (handshake + tools/list).

Pack the NuGet packages

dotnet pack src/BcWordLayout.McpHost -c Release

Produces the top-level BcWordLayout.Mcp package (with the embedded .mcp/server.json
